_about: Field terms for F329, same shape as papers/glossary.json.

reporting-task.definition: an experiment in which a person observes a random outcome in private, such as a die roll or coin toss, reports it, and is paid by the report, so a lie pays and cannot be caught for any one person; lying shows only in the distribution of many reports
reporting-task.excludes: tasks where the experimenter can see each person's true outcome

standardised-report.field: experimental economics; the measure Abeler, Nosenzo and Raymond report, computed here by our own code
standardised-report.definition: the mean report of a treatment after the outcomes are mapped evenly onto -1 for the lowest-paying report and +1 for the highest, so honest reporting gives 0 in expectation and everyone claiming the top gives 1; here averaged over treatments without weights
standardised-report.excludes: a share of liars, which the mean alone does not give

log-loss.definition: minus the average natural log of the probability a model gave to each report that was made; lower is better, and the difference between two models in nats per report is how much better one predicts each report
log-loss.excludes: an accuracy count, which ignores how much probability a model gave to what happened

held-out-papers.definition: papers kept out of all fitting, chosen by a hash of the citation (30 percent of papers), on which every model is scored once; all treatments from one paper fall on the same side
held-out-papers.excludes: a split by treatment or subject, which would let one paper's design appear in both fitting and scoring

maximum-likelihood.definition: fitting a model's parameters by choosing the values that make the observed data most probable under the model
maximum-likelihood.excludes: choosing parameters by hand or by fit to the test data

tremble.definition: a parameter that mixes a share of uniformly random reports into a model's prediction, standing for mistakes and inattention; in these models it is the only source of downward lies
tremble.excludes: a preference, since the tremble does not depend on payoffs

stakes-elasticity.definition: the parameter epsilon in a stakes factor (G/5) to the power 1 minus epsilon, where G is the money at stake; at epsilon 1 the size of the payment has no effect on reports, and at 0 the pull to lie grows in proportion to the payment
stakes-elasticity.excludes: the effect of payment on whether people take part

fixed-point.definition: a report distribution that, when used to compute how honest each report looks, leads people to make the same distribution of reports; found here by repeated damped updates starting from honest reporting
fixed-point.excludes: a guarantee that the fixed point found is the only one

three-part-reading.field: experimental economics, after Fischbacher and Föllmi-Heusi
three-part-reading.definition: a split of a report distribution into honest reporters, read as the number of outcomes times the share reporting the lowest outcome, maximal liars, the excess at the top over the honest share, and partial liars, the rest
three-part-reading.excludes: an observation of any person's lie; it assumes the true outcomes are uniform and that no one lies downward on purpose

climatology.field: forecast verification, where it is called climatology
climatology.definition: a forecast that gives each held-out treatment the average report distribution of training treatments with the same number of outcomes
climatology.excludes: any theory of why people report as they do

sign-permutation-paper.definition: a test that sums each held-out paper's difference in log loss between two models, then flips the sign of each paper's difference at random 5,000 times to see how often a sum as large arises with no true difference
sign-permutation-paper.excludes: a test that treats subjects within one paper as independent

benjamini-hochberg.definition: a rule that adjusts a set of p values so that, among the tests called significant, the expected share of false calls stays at or below a chosen rate q, here 0.05
benjamini-hochberg.excludes: the stricter Bonferroni rule, which bounds the chance of any false call

paper-bootstrap.definition: an interval made by recomputing a statistic 2,000 times on held-out papers drawn with replacement, so subjects from one paper stay together
paper-bootstrap.excludes: resampling single subjects as if they were independent
